title: Search continues after Navy craft incident Off Angulana
byline: Search operations are continuing following the distress incident involving a Sri Lanka Navy Fast Attack Craft off Angulana on August 15, with efforts also underway to salvage the distressed vessel.

title: At least 72 dead, including 18 children, in Zimbabwe ferry disaster
byline: Eighteen children were among more than 70 people killed when an overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe this week, police said Saturday after rescuers recovered more bodies.

title: Man shot dead in Mount Lavinia
byline: A man who was shot and injured on Huludagoda Road in Mount Lavinia has died of his injuries, Police said.

title: 72-hour detention order obtained to question Shiran Basik
byline: The Central Crimes Investigation Bureau (CCIB) has obtained a 72-hour detention order to question alleged large-scale drug trafficker Shiran Basik following his deportation to Sri Lanka from Dubai.

title: Three arrested over viral sword-threat incident in Divulapitiya
byline: Three people have been arrested in connection with an incident in which a bus and a main road were allegedly blocked before a person was threatened with a sword in Divulapitiya.

title: No tsunami threat to Sri Lanka following 6.8-magnitude Indonesia earthquake
byline: The Department of Meteorology has confirmed that there is currently no tsunami threat to Sri Lanka following a 6.8-magnitude earthquake that struck northern Sumatra in Indonesia on Saturday.

title: Second major quake hits Indonesia in a day as 7.7 magnitude tremor leaves 38 dead
byline: A second major earthquake struck Indonesia on Saturday, hours after a powerful 7.7-magnitude quake hit the Flores region, killing at least 38 people and injuring 13 others.

title: Vehicle prices to surge as 50% import duty surcharge extended
byline: Vehicle prices are set to rise further following the Government’s decision to extend the 50% surcharge imposed on vehicle import duties until December 31, the Vehicle Importers Association of Sri Lanka (VIASL) said.

title: Judges’ retirement age: BASL yet to receive complete recording of meeting with President
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has said it is yet to receive the complete video recordings of its recent meeting with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake regarding the proposed constitutional amendment to extend the retirement age of judges of the superior courts.

title: Indonesia quake death toll rises to 38
byline: A 7.7-magnitude earthquake that struck eastern Indonesia on Saturday killed at least 38 people, a disaster management official said, revising an earlier toll.

title: Eleven rescued after fast attack craft runs into distress off Angulana
byline: Eleven crew members of a Sri Lanka Navy fast attack craft that encountered distress in the seas off Angulana have been rescued and admitted to hospital, while one person remains missing, Police said.

title: Search and rescue launched after Navy craft accident
byline: A search and rescue operation has been launched after a Sri Lanka Navy fast attack craft encountered distress in the seas off Angulana while on a routine patrol.

title: Sri Lanka has most favourable view of India globally
byline: Sri Lanka has the most favourable view of India, with 79% of adults expressing a positive opinion, according to a new survey by the Pew Research Center.

title: Trump says he will declare Strait of Hormuz a US ‘territory’ amid Iran war
byline: Control over the waterway has been a sticking point in negotiations between the US and Iran, with Trump’s comments likely to inflame tensions.

title: Alcohol-related health and economic costs exceed tax revenue in Sri Lanka
byline: The health and economic costs associated with alcohol use in Sri Lanka amounted to Rs. 335 billion in 2025, significantly exceeding the Rs. 254 billion collected as income from alcohol taxes during the same year, according to data presented by the Alcohol and Drug Information Centre (ADIC).

title: Legal battles loom against 22nd amendment
byline: Legal battles against the proposed 22nd Amendment are expected to get off the ground next week as the groups in the legal fraternity are expected to file petitions against the legislation as the government prepares to table the legislation in Parliament on August 18. A group of President’s Counsel and the joint opposition are expected to file petitions against the legislation next week.

title: 72-hour detention order issued against drug trafficker Shiran Basik
byline: Sri Lanka Police have obtained a 72-hour detention order against 48-year-old Shiran Basik, identified by police as a major drug trafficker.

title: Sri Lanka to invite international bids later this month
byline: Sri Lanka will finally invite bids from international companies later this month for upstream petroleum development- exploration and extraction of gas and oil- in four blocks of the Mannar basin, Daily Mirror learns.

title: Strengthen criminal justice system before reintroducing death penalty: Criminal Defence Attorney
byline: A senior lawyer specialising in criminal cases and appeals has stressed that Sri Lanka should first strengthen its criminal justice system before considering the reintroduction of the death penalty, warning that an irreversible punishment carries grave risks if investigative and judicial safeguards are inadequate.

title: Indonesia Flores earthquake kills two, tsunami warning lifted after panic
byline: A powerful earthquake struck off Flores, collapsing buildings and prompting evacuations. The brief tsunami alert was lifted, but widespread damage and panic kept authorities on edge.

title: Hatton–Colombo Main Road partially reopened after landslide
byline: One lane of the Hatton–Colombo main road at Kuilwatta, which was completely blocked following a landslide early this morning (15), has now been reopened to traffic.

title: Did Justice Minister record a livestream while driving?
byline: A video of Justice and National Integration Minister Harshana Nanayakkara driving has been falsely presented on social media as footage of him livestreaming while driving on August 13, 2026.

title: Twelve killed and at least 10 injured in Polish bus crash in Hungary
byline: A dozen people were killed and at least 10 injured ​after a Polish bus overturned at night on a motorway ‌in eastern Hungary, Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Sunday morning in a Facebook post.

title: Thousands evacuate after Indonesia quake kills 51, cuts roads
byline: Around 5,000 people have been evacuated after a magnitude-7.7 earthquake smashed an area in eastern Indonesia, killing at least ​51, blocking roads and causing landslides, authorities said on Sunday.

title: Sri Lanka expresses deep sorrow over loss of lives in Indonesian earthquake
byline: Sri Lanka has expressed deep sorrow over the the loss of lives, injuries and devastation caused by the earthquake and aftershocks that struck Flores Island, Indonesia.

title: Bangladesh notch historic first Test win in Australia
byline: Bangladesh continued to impress in the ICC World Test Championship with a superb nine-wicket victory against the current WTC table-toppers Australia in Darwin.

title: Bathing incident in Ma Oya leaves one dead, one missing
byline: A 19-year-old youth has died while another remains missing after three young men got into difficulty while bathing in the Ma Oya in the Madurupitiya area of Meerigama yesterday (15) afternoon.

title: At least 72 dead, including 18 children, in Zimbabwe ferry disaster
byline: Eighteen children were among more than 70 people killed when an overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe this week, police said Saturday after rescuers recovered more bodies.

title: Public approval of the government declines: Verité Research poll
byline: Public approval of the government has declined to 50% as perceptions of Sri Lanka’s economic outlook have weakened, according to the latest ‘Mood of the Nation’ poll conducted by Verité Research.

title: ICC World Test Championship race wide open after Bangladesh stun Australia
byline: The latest ICC World Test Championship (WTC) standings have experienced a significant shake-up following Bangladesh’s sensational victory against table-toppers Australia in Darwin. Delivering one of the most remarkable performances in their Test history, Bangladesh secured a comprehensive nine-wicket triumph over the former world champions, shifting momentum in the ongoing 2025–27 WTC cycle.

title: Navy board probes Angulana craft accident
byline: The Sri Lanka Navy has appointed a special board of inquiry to investigate the sinking of a Fast Attack Craft off the Angulana coast, as search operations continue for a missing naval officer and salvage efforts are underway to recover the vessel.

title: Audit Committee to investigate alleged financial fraud at Nuwara Eliya DS offices
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is set to oversee the appointment of an audit committee to investigate into alleged financial irregularities at the Divisional Secretariat (DS) offices across the Nuwara Eliya District,  Nuwara Eliya District Development Committee Chairman and MP Manjula Suraweeraarachchi said.

title: Twelve killed and at least 10 injured in Polish bus crash in Hungary
byline: A dozen people were killed and at least 10 injured ​after a Polish bus overturned at night on a motorway ‌in eastern Hungary, Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Sunday morning in a Facebook post.

title: Thousands evacuate after Indonesia quake kills 51, cuts roads
byline: Around 5,000 people have been evacuated after a magnitude-7.7 earthquake smashed an area in eastern Indonesia, killing at least ​51, blocking roads and causing landslides, authorities said on Sunday.

title: Delft-bound boat in distress, Navy rescues 10
byline: All 10 people on board a passenger boat that encountered distress while travelling from Kurikattuwan to Delft have been rescued by the Sri Lanka Navy.

title: Rs. 45 bn allocated to complete stalled hospital projects
byline: The government has allocated Rs. 45 billion to restart and complete hospital construction projects that were suspended midway, with the projects expected to be completed within the next two years, Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said.

title: Ukraine attacks Russia with hundreds of drones in one of Kyiv’s largest aerial assaults of the conflict
byline: Russia says it shot down more than 800 Ukrainian drones overnight in what appears to be among Ukraine’s largest aerial attacks on Russia, with authorities reporting at least six people killed.

title: Revised VAT invoice format mandatory from October 1
byline: The revised Value Added Tax (VAT) invoice format will become mandatory from October 1, 2026, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) has announced.

title: Science College produce stunning rugby to lift U-16 Elite Ten-a-Side Cup
byline: Science College produced a superb display of running rugby to dethrone defending champions Wesley College 29-5 in the Cup final of the All Island Under-16 Elite Ten-a-Side Rugby Championship 2026, which concluded at the St. Peter’s College ground in Bambalapitiya.
